readiness_evidence: Hosted replay: on 19/10/26 a Superagent on 0.7.0 (skill 0.55.0) was updated, then its sandbox was reset by the platform (boot id 969a332e... to 9c0fe406..., /root wiped, /app/.agents restored). A fresh conversation reinstalled the tools and the first flow init was refused with persistence_unresolved; the assistant named /app/.agents, the saved bookings came back, flow init then stopped on duplicate_booking_confirmation for the existing Oct 20 booking, and runtime doctor reported survived_restart: true with the boot marker showing both boots (first 969a332e..., last 9c0fe406...). Not shown: a complete new booking after the restart (the Link sign-in expires and was not repeated), and the assistant chose /app/.agents knowing it had survived an earlier reset, so a first-ever install on a new host is still untested.
No request or response exchanged with the registry or with businesses changes. The saved booking file keeps format 2 and no field is added; the only new file is a small note beside the saved state.

The command-line contract of flow init changes: the first init of a runtime now needs --persistent-root or --no-persistent-root. An assistant on an older skill gets a plain-language refusal (persistence_unresolved) that names both flags, so it can recover without the new skill, but it costs one extra call on a runtime that does not yet keep its state in a folder.

Proof that a folder survived a restart uses the machine's boot id, which sandboxes sharing one kernel may report unchanged after a restart. The proof therefore never gives a false yes, but runtime doctor can keep saying a folder is not yet shown to survive when it did.
user_summary: The assistant now sets up saving your bookings and sign-in across restarts when a booking starts, instead of leaving it to chance.
